en: Seasons occur because Earth's axis is tilted 23.5 degrees, causing different hemispheres to receive more direct sunlight at different times of year.
The Moon does not produce its own light; it shines by reflecting sunlight off its rocky, cratered surface.
Lightning can strike flat open ground, bodies of water, or short objects, not only the tallest structures nearby.
Some sedimentary rocks, like shale and chalk, are soft enough to be easily scratched with a fingernail.
Plants contribute to the water cycle through transpiration, releasing water vapor from their leaves into the atmosphere.
Healthy topsoil contains humus from decomposed plants and animals, not just tiny pieces of broken rock.
The Sun generates energy through nuclear fusion, combining hydrogen atoms into helium in its extremely hot core.
Stars appear to twinkle because Earth's moving atmosphere bends their light rays, not because the stars themselves change brightness.
Volcanic eruptions release ash clouds, toxic gases like sulfur dioxide, and fast-moving pyroclastic flows, not just flowing lava.
Venus is hotter than Mercury despite being farther from the Sun, because its thick carbon dioxide atmosphere traps heat.
Clouds consist of millions of tiny liquid water droplets or ice crystals, not invisible water vapor gas.
Earthquakes occur when tectonic plates get stuck at their boundaries and then suddenly snap, releasing stored energy as seismic waves.
